svg.title: NTP as security infrastructure: six mechanisms that depend on it, and the cascade when it fails
svg.desc: Left: one time source feeding six consumers, each with the symptom of a wrong clock. Authentication logs become useless for correlation, and the incident timeline cannot be reconstructed. Certificate validation fails in both directions - a clock behind the validity window gives not yet valid, a clock ahead gives expired - which breaks IPsec, 802.1X and HTTPS management. TACACS+ accounting records the wrong time, so command attribution in an investigation collapses. Two-factor tokens drift and reject valid codes, so people start asking for exceptions. Log correlation across devices is impossible and the first hour of every incident is spent reconciling timestamps. Backup and change windows overlap or run twice. Right: the cascade - NTP unreachable, clocks drift a few minutes, certificates fail, IPsec tunnels drop and supplicants fail to authenticate, the team disables certificate validation or moves to a longer validity window, and the control that was supposed to authenticate peers is now switched off permanently. Bottom: five design rules - at least two sources with different paths, an internal stratum hierarchy rather than every device polling the internet, NTP authentication or at least an ACL, monitoring of the offset itself as a health metric, and a documented fallback that is not the local hardware clock.
svg.text: Time is authentication infrastructure. When it drifts, the controls fail open.
Nobody calls NTP important until certificates start rejecting the peers that were fine yesterday.
NTP source
two, on different paths
Authentication logs
the timeline cannot be reconstructed
Certificates / IPsec / 802.1X
behind = not yet valid, ahead = expired
TACACS+ accounting
"who changed the ACL at 02:00" loses its answer
Two-factor tokens
codes rejected, so exceptions get granted
Cross-device correlation
the first hour of an incident is spent on timestamps
Backup and change windows
run twice, or overlap and corrupt each other
THE CASCADE
1 NTP unreachable, local clock drifts minutes
2 certificates fall outside their validity window
3 IPsec drops, supplicants fail, HTTPS is refused
4 someone disables validation "to restore service"
5 the control is now permanently switched off
Step four is the real damage. The technology failure
is recoverable in an hour; the human workaround is
recoverable only with a second project.
That is why the fallback plan is part of the NTP
design, not part of the incident response.
FIVE DESIGN RULES
two sources on different paths · an internal stratum hierarchy, not every device polling the internet · authentication or an ACL on the NTP server
offset monitored as a health metric, with an alarm · a documented fallback that is not "use the local hardware clock"
Check it in a review: ask what the maximum clock offset in the estate is. If nobody knows, the estate has no time source worth the name.
